operation_safety.method: read-only code trace + read-only local database queries (bounded, indexed) + new isolated unit tests against resolve_creator() with synthetic fixtures. Zero writes to any live B2Z ledger/artifact this milestone.

part2_creator_extraction_code_trace.field_inspected: transaction.message.accountKeys from the jsonParsed getTransaction response for the MIGRATION transaction signature (not the CREATE transaction)
part2_creator_extraction_code_trace.signer_identification: an accountKeys entry is treated as a signer ONLY if it is a dict with key.get('signer') is True. String-only entries (bare pubkey, no signer metadata) are normalized to signer=False by _account_keys() -- they can NEVER be selected as creator via this path.
part2_creator_extraction_code_trace.account_keys_parsing: _account_keys() (lines 112-122) reads transaction.message.accountKeys as a list; for each entry: string -> {pubkey, signer:False}; dict with a string pubkey -> kept as-is (its own signer flag preserved, defaulting to False via .get() if the key is entirely absent). Non-conforming entries are silently dropped from the normalized list (neither error nor included).
part2_creator_extraction_code_trace.jsonparsed_handling: the function assumes the caller already requested encoding=jsonParsed (confirmed at the B2Z dispatch call site: params include {'encoding':'jsonParsed', 'maxSupportedTransactionVersion':0}) -- resolve_creator() itself does no encoding-specific branching, it just reads the standard jsonParsed accountKeys shape
part2_creator_extraction_code_trace.signer_writable_flags: only the 'signer' boolean is consulted; 'writable' is never read or used
part2_creator_extraction_code_trace.static_vs_loaded_addresses: no distinction is made -- loadedAddresses (from address lookup tables, a v0-transaction feature) are NOT separately merged in; only transaction.message.accountKeys is read. If a real migration transaction used an address lookup table for its signer (uncommon but possible), that signer would NOT appear in this field and resolve_creator() would find zero signers, raising B2Z_CREATOR_AMBIGUOUS rather than a wrong answer -- fail-closed, not silently wrong, for that specific case (not the case observed here, since ordinals 3/4/5/7 all resolved successfully, meaning the signer WAS present in accountKeys with signer=True)
part2_creator_extraction_code_trace.pumpfun_program_accounts: no special-casing at all -- the function has no awareness of which accounts are the Pump.fun program, the PumpSwap program, the mint, or any other system account. It relies ENTIRELY on the provider-supplied signer flag.
part2_creator_extraction_code_trace.fee_payer_handling: NOT explicitly identified or special-cased. In Solana, accountKeys[0] is conventionally the fee payer AND is virtually always a signer, but resolve_creator() does not read position -- it only reads the signer flag wherever it appears. Verified by test_fee_payer_position_is_not_special_cased (a signer in the LAST position still resolves correctly).
part2_creator_extraction_code_trace.exactly_one_signer_assumption: HARD requirement, enforced by len(signers) != 1 raising B2Z_CREATOR_AMBIGUOUS. Zero signers, two signers, or any count other than exactly one is rejected -- there is no fallback selection (e.g. 'pick the first signer', 'pick accountKeys[0]') for the ambiguous case.
part2_creator_extraction_code_trace.fallback_default_behavior: NONE. Every non-single-signer or malformed-input case raises a ValueError (B2Z_MINT_NOT_IN_MIGRATION, B2Z_CREATOR_AMBIGUOUS, B2Z_MIGRATION_TIME_MISSING, or B2Z_ACCOUNT_KEYS_MALFORMED from _account_keys). There is no silent default value returned.
part2_creator_extraction_code_trace.index_assumptions: none beyond requiring the mint's own pubkey to be present somewhere in accountKeys (order-independent, uses a set membership check)

part3_raw_evidence_inspection.method: already-persisted stage outputs only (docs/audits/b2z_p1_stage_outputs_b2z-p1-44d6798563468c8aff747446.json), cross-referenced against token_analysis and pumpfun_migration_verification. NO new provider calls. The full raw transaction JSON (accountKeys array with signer flags) was NOT independently re-derivable from any local source, because B2Z's durable design deliberately never persists full raw provider response bodies (see B2ZStageOutputLedger docstring: 'never full provider response bodies') and the tf_transaction_cache read-only adapter had ZERO cache hits for any of these 5 migration signatures (checked directly).
part3_raw_evidence_inspection.dex_confirmation: all 4 affected migration_tx signatures independently confirmed present in pumpfun_migration_verification with dex='pumpswap' and 4 DIFFERENT pumpswap_pool_address values -- these are 4 genuinely distinct migration events, not duplicate/reused signatures
part3_raw_evidence_inspection.signer_flag_and_account_keys_detail: NOT independently re-derivable from any local source (see method note above) -- resolve_creator() only persists the FINAL resolved creator+blockTime into the stage-output ledger, by design, never the full accountKeys/signer array. This is an acknowledged LIMIT of this local-only investigation, disclosed explicitly rather than papered over.

part4_signer_role_determination.is_the_repeated_address_actually_a_signe: PROVEN INDIRECTLY, not directly observed: resolve_creator() would have raised B2Z_CREATOR_AMBIGUOUS for ordinals 3/4/5/7 if the address were NOT the sole signer=True entry (this is the function's only success path, confirmed exactly by code trace in Part 2 and by the isolated unit tests in Part 11). Since all 4 ordinals returned STAGE_COMPLETE for MIGRATION_TX with this creator, it MUST have been the sole signer=True entry in each of the 4 raw transactions at the time of dispatch.
part4_signer_role_determination.is_it_fee_payer: cannot be independently confirmed from local data (position not persisted) -- but signer status alone is Solana-typical of a fee payer, and B2Z's own historical caveat (B2Z-P1.6) speculated exactly this role
part4_signer_role_determination.is_it_a_pumpfun_system_program_account: NO -- confirmed the address is a genuine ordinary wallet, not a program account: it is independently the pf_ws_creator (CREATE-transaction creator/fee-payer) for 7 real, unrelated tokens in the local database (query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM token_analysis WHERE pf_ws_creator=... -> 7), and it receives (never sends) SOL via transfer_index 4 times. A Solana program account cannot legitimately sign as a Pump.fun token creator elsewhere -- this rules out hypothesis D (Pump.fun/migration/system program account) definitively.
part4_signer_role_determination.same_account_index_each_time: not determinable without the raw accountKeys array (see Part 3 disclosed limit)
part4_signer_role_determination.controls_or_relates_to_all_four_launches: NO evidence it created, controls, or is otherwise administratively related to mints for ordinals 3/4/5/7 -- their pf_ws_creator/earliest_tx_creator values are 4 DIFFERENT addresses, all distinct from 9C4nRvhhVquC..., and creator_mismatch=0 for the (spot-checked) mints, meaning the production pipeline's OWN creator-consistency check found no conflict for those tokens using ITS OWN methodology
part4_signer_role_determination.broader_frequency_appearance: appears as pf_ws_creator (i.e. genuine CREATE-tx creator) for 7 DIFFERENT, UNRELATED tokens locally -- none of which are ordinals 3/4/5/7's mints. This is the single strongest piece of evidence: the address is a real, independently-token-creating wallet, seen here in an ENTIRELY DIFFERENT role (migration signer) for tokens it did not create.

part5_create_vs_migration_creator_compar.both_legitimate_actors_different_roles: YES, strongly supported -- the CREATE-derived creator is a distinct real wallet for each mint (production pipeline's own creator_mismatch=0 check found no internal conflict for these values, spot-checked), while the migration-derived signer is a SEPARATE, independently-verified real wallet (creates 7 of its OWN other tokens elsewhere) that appears to act as an agent triggering migration for tokens it did not create.
part5_create_vs_migration_creator_compar.not_assumed_local_creator_wrong: explicitly NOT assumed -- the CREATE-tx creator remains a valid, well-established concept (documented as the primary creator-tracking methodology throughout docs/CLAUDE.md and the repository's production funding-extraction pipeline). This finding does not invalidate the local prediction; it reveals that B2Z's contract is measuring a DIFFERENT thing.
part5_create_vs_migration_creator_compar.does_b2z_contract_truly_intend_migration: this is answered directly in Part 6 below using the repository's own prior documentation, not assumed here

part6_governing_b2z_semantics.authoritative_source: docs/audits/b2z_p1_6_historical_creator_funding_data_lineage_reconstruction.json, field part4_writer_traced.critical_distinction_from_b2z (written during an EARLIER milestone, BEFORE this live discrepancy was ever observed)
part6_governing_b2z_semantics.exact_quote: "B2Z's resolve_creator() derives creator from the MIGRATION transaction's unique signer. The production pipeline derives pf_ws_creator from the CREATE transaction's fee payer/signer. On Pump.fun these are very likely the same wallet in the overwhelming majority of cases (a token's creator typically also owns/triggers its own migration), but this is a STRUCTURAL, UNPROVEN ASSUMPTION relative to B2Z's specific contract -- not something this reconstruction can treat as equivalent without qualification."
part6_governing_b2z_semantics.what_b2z_means_by_creator: EXPLICITLY, by design: the migration transaction's sole signer. Not the CREATE-transaction creator, not the bonding-curve authority, not a launch-authority concept -- specifically and only 'whoever signed the transaction that moved this token from Pump.fun's bonding curve to a PumpSwap pool'.
part6_governing_b2z_semantics.does_implementation_match_contract: YES -- resolve_creator() implements EXACTLY the documented single-signer-of-migration-tx concept, with no deviation found in Part 2's code trace. There is no bug in the implementation relative to its own stated contract.
part6_governing_b2z_semantics.was_this_gap_known_in_advance: YES, explicitly, in writing, before this milestone -- this is not a newly-discovered ambiguity, it is the DOCUMENTED, PREDICTED failure mode of a previously-flagged unproven assumption, now observed manifesting for 4 of 7 resolved eligible members in the live cohort (57% of the resolved-so-far sample, though this is far too small a sample to generalize a global rate from).

part7_broader_frequency_check.as_migration_signer_for_unrelated_tokens: NOT MEASURED -- would require either the raw migration-tx accountKeys for a large population (not locally cached, would need live RPC, explicitly prohibited this milestone) or a dedicated local index of migration-transaction signers, which does not currently exist in this repository (only migration_tx SIGNATURES are indexed in pumpfun_migration_verification, not their signer). This is a genuine, disclosed evidence gap -- the true global frequency of this address as a migration signer across ALL Pump.fun migrations cannot be determined from local data alone.
part7_broader_frequency_check.conclusion: local evidence is consistent with (but does not conclusively prove beyond the 4 observed cases) a shared migration-completion-agent role. The 7-tokens-created-elsewhere fact, combined with zero outbound transfers and some inbound transfers, paints a wallet that is NOT a program account and IS an active participant in the Pump.fun ecosystem, plausibly in an automated migration-triggering capacity for tokens beyond its own.

part8_classification.reasoning: resolve_creator()'s implementation exactly matches its own documented contract (migration-tx sole signer), with no code defect found. The repeated address is confirmed to be a real, independently-verified wallet (not a program/system account), genuinely creating 7 other tokens elsewhere -- ruling out both B2Z_CREATOR_EXTRACTION_BUG (the code does what it says) and the 'Pump.fun/system account misidentified as signer' variant of option D. The finding is that B2Z's contract concept of 'creator' (migration-tx signer) and the production pipeline's concept (CREATE-tx creator) are GENUINELY DIFFERENT ROLES that happen to diverge for this specific address across 4 of the cohort's tokens -- exactly the previously-documented, previously-flagged risk. This is closest to option A+D combined in the original hypothesis list, refined with actual evidence: A is true in the sense that the address IS a genuine, real actor (not noise/bug), but D's 'program account' framing is specifically ruled out -- it is better described as a genuine shared AGENT (likely automated migration bot/service), not a program.
